articles.title: Meet the insanely hot male stars of 'The Shards,' Ryan Murphy's new gay thriller
articles.description: Ryan Murphy ’s buzzy new show The Shards is already off to an amazing start after premiering on August 5. Star Igby Rigney has gone viral for a scene where he was only sporting a pair of white underwear , and everyone is talking about the steamy show and its hot stars. Set in 1980s Los Angeles, The Shards is based on a Bret Easton Ellis novel of the same name. It follows the prep school student Bret, whose privileged life begins to unravel when he meets the enigmatic new student Robert. Things get complicated as Bret navigates teenage drama, drug-fueled excess, and secret sexual relationships with his male classmates, all while a serial killer known as “The Trawler” begins terrorizing the city. Murphy is known for his soapy gay dramas, and The Shards is living up to this reputation. Full of dramatic tension, excess-soaked parties, and plenty of steamy sex, The Shards is proving to be the perfect summer escape. The show’s first season has only just begun, but fans are already hooked. The ‘80s hair, fashion, and sets — combined with the sexy and thrilling plot — make it must-watch TV. You would also be forgiven if you’re mostly glued to your screen because of the hunky stars. But just who are these hot young stars and where else can you see them? Meet the boys ahead! And catch new episodes of The Shards Wednesdays on FX and Hulu. Igby Rigney See on Instagram Igby Rigney is playing the lead character, Bret, a 17-year-old fictionalized version of Bret Easton Ellis, who has an on-again, off-again relationship with Debbie (Hayes Warner) while having secret gay rendezvous with male classmates. Rigney is best known for starring in Mike Flanagan’s Netflix series Midnight Mass , The Midnight Club , and The Fall of the House of Usher . See on Instagram See on Instagram Homer Gere See on Instagram Homer Gere is starring as Robert Mallory, the enigmatic, privileged new student at the fictional Buckley prep school, whose entrance upends Bret’s life. Aside from being Richard Gere’s son, Homer Gere also starred as Dylan Reid in four episodes of Euphoria . See on Instagram See on Instagram Graham Campbell See on Instagram Graham Campbell plays star football player Thom Wright, who is one half of the archetypal high school couple alongside Susan Reynolds (Kaia Gerber). Prior to starring in The Shards , Campbell was in the Willem Dafoe film Late Fame . See on Instagram See on Instagram Owen Painter See on Instagram Owen Painter stars as Matt Kellner, one of Bret’s close friends. He is a laid-back, weed-smoking teen who has a secret sexual relationship with Bret. Prior to The Shards , Painter starred in an episode of The Handmaid’s Tale , the miniseries Tiny Beautiful Things , and played Slurp in Netflix’s Wednesday . See on Instagram See on Instagram Wes Bentley See on Instagram Wes Bentley plays Hollywood mogul Terry Schaffer, the father of Brett’s girlfriend Debbie, who tries to seduce Bret with promises of hiring him as a screenwriter. Bentley has had a long and storied career in Hollywood that started with his breakthrough role in American Beauty and has continued for decades. He also starred in Interstellar , The Hunger Games , Mission Impossible: Fallou t , and played main character Jamie Dutton on the hit series Yellowstone . See on Instagram See on Instagram

articles.title: Halloween: The Game Banned In Australia, But Murdering People Isn’t The Problem
articles.description: Halloween: The Game is right around the corner, but fans of the old-school horror film series in Australia and New Zealand won't be allowed to take part when the game comes out next month. Developer Illfonic has confirmed that it has been denied classification in those countries, effectively ruling it out from being sold legally within those regions. The strange thing is the reason behind the denial for classification, as it's not because players can take control of a stab-happy murderer who indiscriminately kills kids and adults. Instead, the reason behind the banning is because of the "presence of a controlled substance," according to the social media account for Halloween: The Game. "Despite every effort on our part, the Australian Classification Board has denied 'Halloween: The Game' a rating," the account confirmed . "The denial was not based on the presence of the iconic slasher, Michael Myers, or the outstanding kills that can be performed in the game, but rather the presence of a controlled substance. Unfortunately, to our disappointment--and certainly yours--this means that we cannot sell the physical or digital product in both Australia and New Zealand." https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jhkesn3VX8k Australia is notorious for refusing to classify video games , as hundreds of titles like Hotline Miami , Saints Row 4, and South Park: The Stick of Truth have run afoul of its ratings group, the Australian Classification Board. According to law, any work deemed too inappropriate and featuring content that violates certain guidelines could be refused classification. It's also mandatory for games to be classified in that country. While many games weren't allowed to be sold on that side because of extreme violence--like the 2011 Mortal Kombat reboot--recent titles that featured drug use and sexual activity with characters who appear to be under 18 appear to be the main reason for being refused classification . Meanwhile, Halloween: The Game will launch worldwide--except for the folks down under--on September 8, for PC and console. Inspired by the classic 1978 slasher movie, players can either don the modified William Shatner mask of Michael Myers or play as the everyday citizens of Haddonfield in their quest to survive the night against the malevolent Shape of evil. 30 Best Horror Games To Play In The Dark In 2026 View Images

articles.title: Harry Potter Fans Force $580M Project to Move to Protect Character’s Grave
articles.description: Alexander Demianchuk / Reuters Harry Potter fans have successfully pushed a $580 million power project to change course after discovering that an underground cable could pass through the spot where Dobby, the fictional house elf, was buried in the film series. Dobby was killed and laid to rest on Freshwater West beach in Pembrokeshire, Wales, in Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows . The location has since become an unofficial memorial for fans, who regularly leave stones inscribed with messages such as “Here lies Dobby” despite the fact that the National Trust, which owns the land, discourages the practice because the beach is an ecologically sensitive area. They also used to leave socks, because Potter uses a sock to trick Lucius Malfoy into giving Dobby his freedom. Read more at The Daily Beast.
